title: CNBC live on the Meta Ray-Ban Display: a proxy in front of a Referer-gated CDN
metaDescription: Live CNBC on 600x600 glasses with a D-pad: the interesting engineering is the local proxy that re-arbitrates the CDN host and rewrites the playlist to same-origin URLs.
dek: A live CNBC stream on 600x600 glasses with D-pad navigation only — and a local proxy that exists because the upstream CDN only serves its playlist to the right Referer.
intro: This project puts a live CNBC feed on the Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses: a 600x600 viewport, D-pad only, streaming from a free feed that needs no login. The player is not the interesting part. The upstream CDN only serves its playlist when the request carries the right Referer header, which a glasses webview cannot fake, so a small local proxy sits in front of it: it re-arbitrates the best CDN host and caches that choice with a long TTL, rewrites the playlist so every segment URL is same-origin, and streams the bytes through without ever buffering a whole segment in memory.
why: On a wearable, the buffering is the product: time-to-first-frame is the feature, which forces a streaming design rather than a download-then-play one. Understanding the constraint before optimising the code is what made the proxy small — an upstream Referer gate is the entire reason it exists. The tuning is all on a weak link: prewarm the host arbitration at startup so the cold path is not the startup delay, and never hard-seek on a stall, because jumping back to the live edge throws the buffer away and turns a dip into a loop. The wrong watchdog can make playback measurably worse than no watchdog at all.

faq.q: Why is there a proxy at all?
faq.a: Because the upstream CDN only serves its playlist when the request carries the right Referer header, which a glasses webview cannot fake. A local proxy stands in front, re-arbitrates and caches the best CDN host, rewrites the playlist to same-origin URLs and streams the bytes through.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: $0 for the feed and the code — there are no model calls and the stream is free. The only billable resource is the machine running the proxy.

faq.q: What was the hard part on a wearable?
faq.a: Time-to-first-frame. Streaming the bytes instead of reading a whole segment into memory, prewarming host arbitration, and not hard-seeking on a stall: the wrong watchdog measurably worsens playback compared with leaving it alone.
